Inclusion and SEND Curriculum
Our Vision at Holyport is to offer a curriculum driven through the lens of developing a love of learning and life and to achieve this to the fullest, as individual and collectively.
'I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full.' John 10.10b
Our vision is to provide all of our pupils with opportunities to excel, develop and flourish; we do this through offering high quality enriching experiences that in turn inform the quality of our creative curriculum and inform our school values.
We wish our children a life of abundance; abundance is an appreciation of life in its fullness so when they leave us, they are responsible , caring and active citizens for the future.
Our vision statement: Rooted in our Christian Foundation everyone feels valued, respected and knows their contribution will be recognised. Through our broad and memorable education experiences, all pupils achieve their full potential and become enthusiastic learners for life. Our pupils are active, healthy, responsible citizens of the future.
As a school, we aim to ensure that all children are provided with high quality learning experiences based on a broad, balanced and creative curriculum. Holyport CE Primary School is committed to inclusion with policies and practices that include all learners. We are dedicated to providing a personalised and high-quality education to all our children. Diversity is valued as a rich resource and we believe that all children, including those identified as having special educational needs and disabilities, have a common entitlement to a broad and balanced academic and social curriculum which is accessible to them, and to be fully included in all aspects of school life.
Inclusion is an on-going process and involves the identification and minimising of the barriers to learning and participation that may be experienced by any child, irrespective of age, ability, gender, ethnicity, language or social background and the maximising of resources to reduce such barriers. We strive to avoid the isolation of children and encourage collaborative learning and peer tutoring. We provide learning opportunities that are absorbing, creative, rewarding and effectively differentiated with diverse teaching styles.
Every pupil with SEND and/or others who could be at risk of social exclusion, have an entitlement to fulfil his/her optimum potential. This is achieved by ensuring the wellbeing of all pupils in relation to: being healthy, staying safe, enjoying and achieving, making a positive contribution, and achieving social and economic well-being. These outcomes are embraced in every aspect of school life through personalised teaching and learning approaches.
Support for emotional wellbeing is provided through ELSA support as well as flexible or individualised timetables and assessment for learning which engages pupils in reflecting on their progress.
Partnership with parents/carers, other schools, professional, the local community, health care and social service providers is embraced and sought.
Our Curriculum is creative and inclusive, children can access and engage with their peers irrespective of their needs.
Please see our SEND Local Offer and more information on the range of support we can provide on our Children pages

Information About Our Governors
Amanda Featherstone - Headteacher
I have been the Headteacher at Holyport C of E Primary School and on the Governing Body since September 2016. With a teaching career of 23 years, I am totally committed to providing the children at Holyport with the best education and opportunities that I can, working together with the whole school and local community. I believe my role is to work together with our team of dedicated Governors and continuously improve the school.
Claire Birtles - Foundation Governor (Term of Office 10/03/2026 - 09/03/2030)
I am an MFL and Humanities teacher at a local middle school and have been involved with governing bodies in many different schools as a clerk over the past decade. I see my work with young people as a vocation and I have always had a deep-seated interest in the education the whole child. I am a committed Christian and I look forward to becoming involved in the spiritual life of this school. I am a member of the Standards and Staffing committee, and the Link Governor for RE.
Alex Drewett - Co-opted Governor (Term of Office 06/05/2025 - 05/05/2027)
I grew up in Holyport and continue to have a close family connection to the village. Professionally I work as a GP and I have experience working in policy and strategy at the Royal College of General Practitioners. I have a professional interest in medical education and previously I have worked as a Medical Education Fellow for Health Education England monitoring standards of training for post-graduate doctors. I hope that my professional and lived experience can help support the school in providing the best education for all of its pupils. I am a member of the Standards and Staffing, and Finance, Marketing, Premises and Pay committees, and am the Link Governor for DT, EYFS and Geography.
Zoe James - Parent Governor (Term of Office 31/01/2024 - 30/01/2028)
I am pleased to join the board as a Parent Governor, and have one child at the school. I am a class teacher myself and have a wellbeing role in my current school, which in the independent prep sector. With many years of teaching behind me, I look forward to helping support Holyport C of E Primary School to provide the best education possible for our children. I am a member of the Admissions, and Standards and Staffing committees, and am the Link Governor for LAC, PPG, and SEND, as well as PE, PSHE and Wellbeing.
Lynda Jones - Foundation Governor (Term of Office 19/11/2024 - 18/11/2028)
I have been a Foundation Governor for 8 years. I am a member of the Finance, Marketing, Premises and Pay committee, and the Admissions committee. I am also the Link
Governor for Safeguarding, E-Safety and Whistleblowing.
Shannon Keenlyside - Foundation Governor (Term of Office 14/11/2023 - 13/11/2027)
I am a Foundation Governor, and Chair of the Standards and Staffing committee. I also sit on the Admissions committee. I am Link Governor for English and Modern Foreign Languages, as well as Equality. My eldest daughter attended the school. I work as a freelance editor of primary school educational resources.
Catherine Kelly - Staff Governor (Term of Office 04/11/25 - 03/11/29)
I am an HLTA (Higher Level Teaching Assistant) at the school and have two children who both joined Holyport Primary School in Reception. I am passionate about the school and its place in the community, and I am excited to take on this role. My previous career was as an Account Manager, and I have also had a long-standing professional interest in psychology and child development. I am a member of the Admissions committee, and the Standards and Staffing committee.
Paul Mew - Community Governor/Chair of the Governing Body (Term of Office 23/11/2023 - 22/11/2027)
I started as a Parent Governor, and am now a Community Governor - I have three boys who all started in Reception at the school. I am privileged to be current Chair of Governors, and Chair of the Admissions committee. I also sit on the Finance, Marketing, Premises and Pay committee. I am the Link Governor for Behaviour, Health and Safety, Computing, Maths, and Science. My day job is Technical Director of an IT company.
Father Ainsley Swift - Foundation Governor (Term of Office 30/06/2026 - 29/06/2030)
I originally trained to be a teacher and then had a career in Community Development with a number of projects including working for The Children's Society all in the Liverpool area. I was Ordained in the Church of England in 1994 and have been ministering in the Parishes covering central Windsor for the last 20 years. I became the Vicar of Bray and joined the Governing Body at Holyport in July 2018. I am the Link Governor for Collective Worship, and RE. I sit on the Standards and Staffing committee.
Melanie White - Parent Governor (Term of Office 26/06/2024 - 25/06/2028)
As a parent of two children attending the school I am really excited to be a part of the Governor team, as well as a committee member of the HSA. I am a qualified accountant with a senior finance role in a large organisation - I am pleased to bring this experience to the Governor team and to take on the role as Chair of the Finance, Marketing, Premises and Pay committee. I also sit on the Standards and Staffing committee, and am the Link Governor for History and Music.

Important Information
Each child has been given a reading record to take home and bring into school daily with their reading book. We would like children to record the name of the book they are reading, how many pages they have read on a particular date, and a brief comment on how well they read aloud or what they thought of the text/what happened, and to have this signed by an adult daily. We would like children to aim to read for at least 10 minutes, five times a week. There will be whole-school initiatives to encourage children in their reading. We will also be reading our class text daily, giving different members of the class an opportunity to read aloud.
For each half-termly topic, there is a homework grid for children to select tasks from. This grid will be placed at the bottom of the class page in case a hard copy is lost. These tasks are rated as Bronze, Silver or Gold. House points are awarded for each (Bronze = 1HP, Silver = 2HP, Gold = 3HP) and we encourage the children to complete as many as possible.
Some tasks can be completed in homework books, others need to be presented neatly on plain or lined paper, ready for display in the classroom or in our Year 5/6 corridor. If a task is not fully completed or is not presented to the best of the child's ability, they may be asked to re-do the task. We wish for the children to take pride in the work they do.
